meta.title: ALSAP Foundations: Thinking at the Asset Level

props.text: ALSAP exists because safety oversight is not static. As an asset moves through development, safety knowledge accumulates, changes, and sometimes contradicts earlier assumptions.
ALSAP provides a structured way to plan how safety data will be monitored, assessed, and revisited over time so that safety decisions are intentional, consistent, and defensible.
ALSAP is not primarily about compliance. It is about coherent safety thinking over time.
Asset-level thinking means stepping back from individual studies, datasets, or events and asking a different question: What do these signals collectively mean for the future of this asset?

items.title: Across Studies
items.body: Considers multiple studies rather than isolated results.

items.title: Across Populations
items.body: Looks at safety patterns across different patient groups.

items.title: Across Time
items.body: Accounts for how safety knowledge evolves over development phases.

items.title: Across Patterns
items.body: Focuses on interpretation, not simple aggregation.

props.text: Asset-level does not mean everything. It means the information that materially informs safety understanding and decision-making for the asset as a whole.

items.title: Other Safety Documents
items.body: Define study-specific monitoring, protocol procedures, and detailed statistical analysis.

items.title: ALSAP
items.body: Defines how safety will be monitored and assessed at the asset level, including what is reviewed, when, and why.

props.text: ALSAP does not replace other safety documents. It provides the asset-level frame that connects them.
Safety Topics of Interest are the backbone of ALSAP. A STOI is not simply a list of adverse events.

items.title: Plausible Concern
items.body: Grounded in mechanism, data, or emerging signal.

items.title: Decision-Relevant
items.body: Has the potential to influence safety decisions.

props.text: Not every observation is a STOI, and not every STOI requires escalation. Judgment is required.
ALSAP is intentionally structured, but it is not a checklist.
There will be moments where data are incomplete, signals are ambiguous, or experts disagree.
ALSAP does not provide answers in these moments. It provides a framework for disciplined judgment and documentation of rationale.

items.title: ALSAP Lead
items.body: Coordinates the process and ensures coherence.

items.title: Contributing Authors
items.body: Provide domain expertise from their functional areas.

items.title: SMT Members
items.body: Provide oversight and make safety decisions.

props.text: Alignment does not mean agreement. It means shared understanding of rationale.

scenes.title: What ALSAP Is and Is Not

props.text: What ALSAP Is and Is Not

items.title: ALSAP Is
items.body: A planning tool, coordination mechanism, and record of safety intent and rationale.

items.title: ALSAP Is Not
items.body: A checklist, a guarantee against safety issues, or a static compliance document.

props.question: Which statement best reflects the purpose of ALSAP?

options.text: To ensure all safety documents follow the same template
To support coherent, asset-level safety thinking and decision-making over time
To replace other safety monitoring documents

feedback.correct: Correct. ALSAP supports coherent, asset-level safety thinking and decision-making.
feedback.incorrect: ALSAP is not primarily about templates or replacing other documents.
